sources.source: Latest telecoms and pay-TV complaints revealed - Q4 2025
sources.role: Quarterly complaint rates describe provider service-quality signals and cannot establish physical broadband availability, live orderability or measured speed for a selected parcel.

sources.source: Broadband complaints fall to record low
sources.role: Complaint volumes and provider rankings are service-quality context and cannot verify selected-parcel network coverage, orderability or measured performance.

sources.source: Social tariffs: Cheaper broadband and phone packages
sources.role: Tariff eligibility, advertised prices and package speeds are commercial offer information and do not establish availability or measured speed at a selected parcel.

sources.source: Money saving tips for phone, broadband and pay-TV
sources.role: Consumer savings guidance and commercial package comparisons do not establish selected-parcel broadband coverage, orderability or measured speed.

sources.source: Comparing customer service: choosing the best home broadband, mobile and landline provider
sources.role: Customer-satisfaction, complaints-handling and provider operational metrics are aggregate service-quality evidence and cannot establish selected-parcel broadband availability or measured speed.

sources.source: Project Gigabit National Rolling Open Market Review May 2026
sources.role: Open Market Review submissions describe supplier-reported existing and planned build over a three-year horizon; they require formal assessment and exact UPRN/current-service validation before any parcel promotion.

sources.source: Closure of the May 2026 National Rolling Open Market Review
sources.role: The closure notice records an assessment workflow and future publication of postcode and UPRN outputs; it is not itself exact current selected-parcel service evidence.

sources.source: Project Gigabit National Rolling Open Market Review January 2026
sources.role: The January review is a dated supplier-submission and planning process; exact regional file, UPRN, schema and current-service validation remain required for parcel promotion.
Voucher eligibility and grant rules support intervention assessment but do not prove a network is built, orderable or measured at a selected parcel.
The evaluation plan describes programme design, research phases and remote public-building interventions; it cannot establish current surrounding-parcel broadband orderability or speed.
National programme targets, definitions and intervention mechanisms are aggregate policy context and cannot establish current selected-parcel serviceability or measured speed.

sources.authority: Building Digital UK / Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
sources.role: Process-review findings and programme outputs are evaluation evidence; they do not prove current broadband availability or measured performance for nearby selected parcels.
Operator deployment plans are forecasts and aggregate projections; exact selected-parcel availability requires current premises-level archive and orderability validation.

sources.role: Consumer guidance, estimated checker speeds and technology bands do not establish exact current serviceability or measured speed at a selected parcel.
